messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: model-load failures in eu-west-1 serving pool. Pattern: repeated OOM during init, followed by container restarts. Auto-escalation -> paging oncall.
maria: I'm on it, looking at the failing node list now. Seeing many pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff with kernel messages referencing `cuda: out of memory` at load.
jake: Node-level note: one host shows a GPU reset event and `nvidia-driver` churn. Could be driver+kernel combo.
maria: grabbing a sample log from pod model-loader-7f9b: ```stderr
E tensorflow: failed to deserialize weights: zlib checksum mismatch
E runtime: cuda: driver api error: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
E loader: allocate failed: attempted 16.0GiB, available 12.3GiB
```
sam: Can we fail traffic to the fallback variant? Suggest routing affected model name -> quantized-2x fallback in eu-west-1 and divert new loads to eu-central-1 for hot reloads.
lina: Customer impact: several sandbox accounts reported 503s, three paying customers (acct IDs sent to sec channel) seeing request timeouts >10s. No SLO breach yet but elevated error rate.
maria: I'm initiating a rolling drain of the most-affected nodes and will cordon + evict to drain KV caches safely. Plan: 1) cordon nodes with >3 restarts 2) restart GPU driver on remaining suspect nodes 3) pin new loads to fallback variant.
jake: Driver restart command I used earlier: ```bash
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service
# follow with /usr/local/bin/gpu-health-check || echo gpu-fail
```
sam: Doing a canary: redirecting 10% of traffic for model X -> quantized-2x, 90% stays on primary but with circuit-breaker at 5s. Monitoring latency and error rate.
maria: Observed one pod failing during deserialization with stack: `runtime: compile timeout after 45s while JITing operator kernel` — looks like compile-time latency for some kernels on older GPUs. Triggering a compile-cache warmup for those kernels on the fallback nodes.
lina: I'll prepare a customer comms snippet. Short blurb: "We're investigating model load failures causing transient errors in eu-west-1; we've applied mitigations and traffic is being routed to a fallback model to reduce impact. We'll update in 30m"
jake: If driver restarts don't stabilize, we should failover the whole serving pool to eu-central and mark eu-west-1 for deeper infra triage.
maria: Driver restarts completed on 3 nodes, one node still flapping (OOM at init). Draining it now and spinning up replacement from warm pool.
sam: Metrics: error_rate for model X dropped from 8% -> 2.1% after 10% diversion. Latency p95 improved by ~1.2s on canary.
lina: ETA for next update: 15m. I'll escalate to outages channel if we cross 5% errors or any customer reports data loss.
maria: Followups: collect full dmesg + /var/log/nvidia* from flapping host and attach to incident ticket. Also adding `--disable-jit` flag to loader on fallback nodes as temporary to avoid compile timeouts.
jake: noted. tagging infra for driver matrix: @infra-team please correlate kernel/driver versions on eu-west batch.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status -> mitigation in progress; paged teams: infra, oncall, devrel. Logs aggregated at https://internal.logs/redwood/incident/4612345678
